name: @ai-atomic-framework/cli
description: CLI entrypoint for AI-Atomic-Framework repository adoption and validation.

budget.semantics: ACC-3 vs this unmodified Phase-2 inventory: unpacked CLI bytes must fall at least 70% (remain <= 3365772) and entry count at least 80% (remain <= 308). The budget is a cap. Forbidden classes stay rejected even if they would fit.

runtimeClosure.rationale: The CLI is the single published npm product. Transpiled CLI modules reach sibling workspaces through relative specifiers that escape packages/cli, so a tarball carrying only packages/cli/dist resolved nothing. Sibling runtime output is vendored under dist/_vendor in the packages/<name>/ layout, which keeps intra-vendor specifiers valid and leaves only the CLI's own escaping specifiers to rewrite.

supersededBudgets.reason: The sealed 70%/80% target is not feasible without removing live command modules. The owner authorized a bounded quickfix/emergency completion path; preserve runtime behavior while enforcing a measured cap and rejecting development-only payloads.

ownerApprovedDependencyRevision.reason: Owner directed the single public CLI tarball product closure: converge the npm release from 27 public workspaces to one self-contained CLI. Vendoring sibling runtime output into dist/_vendor is the direct and intended cost of that closure, so the cap is re-based on the measured self-contained artifact rather than on the multi-package layout it replaces. The forbidden classes below stay rejected at the new cap.

forbiddenArtifacts.reason: Not mapped to a runtime entrypoint.
Dogfood/CI only; must not pack as adopter runtime.
Runtime evidence must not ship as adopter source content.
Developer kit (src) must not be a runtime dependency once dist exists. This proposal does not mutate /files.
